name: Cosmo 'Cosmic' Chandler
biography:
Cosmo Chandler was supposed to be a priest in the Solarian Empire's state religion, but he was expelled from seminary for asking too many questions about why the divine would create infinite variety if the empire only wanted one way of living. He found his true calling in exploration, treating every new system as a theological text to be read and interpreted rather than a resource to be exploited. The nickname 'Cosmic' started as a gentle joke about his tendency to view everything through a spiritual lens, but Cosmo embraced it completely—he believes that understanding the cosmos is the highest form of worship, and that the universe speaks to those willing to listen. He's particularly interested in the ruins of ancient civilizations, and he's spent more time studying alien temples than mining asteroids. Other explorers sometimes find him impractical, but none can deny that his discoveries have fundamentally changed how humanity understands its place in the universe.

Cosmo speaks in the soft, reflective tones of someone who's always half-listening for something ineffable and vast. He has the educated accent of the Solarian priestly caste, but his speech is filled with pauses, qualifiers, and philosophical asides that can frustrate practical-minded listeners. He never makes statements about what things are—only about what they might mean, and he treats every discovery, no matter how small, as an invitation to wonder. When examining an alien artifact, he sounds like he's delivering a sermon: 'Do you feel it? The weight of intention in this object? Whatever civilization created this didn't build it for utility—they built it to say something about who they were, what they believed, what they feared. We're not just examining metal and stone; we're communing with the dead, learning from those who watched the same stars we do, millions of years ago. This isn't just exploration—it's resurrection. We give them voice again, if only we're wise enough to listen.'
